lines.text: On the practice-room wall hangs an old board of bells, numbered one to five. When a bell rings, everyone in the house knows exactly who’s wanted.
Your thumb is 1, on both hands.
Then one hand is back to front!
Put your palms together. 1 meets 1, and 5 meets 5, like a mirror. Going up the keys, the right hand plays 1 2 3 4 5, and the left hand plays 5 4 3 2 1.
A true story from music history.

Long ago, lots of keyboard players hardly used their thumbs at all. The thumb just dangled below the keys. Then, in 1753, Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach, one of Johann Sebastian Bach’s sons, wrote a famous book about playing the keyboard. In it he said that his father had made the thumb a proper working finger.
These days the thumb gets the best number of all. It’s number 1.
Thumbs are 1 in both hands. The numbers mirror.
